question_record.context: As part of a recent security incident, a Windows executable file that had been renamed was launched on the host `mb-adfs`. The file executed was `iy2orr1e.rrg.exe` with process ID 3116, an action that could indicate malicious intent such as running unauthorized code or connecting to an attacker-controlled network address. Following this, a malicious PowerShell Cmdlet was invoked, which could be associated with credential theft or network reconnaissance. Ultimately, emails containing a malicious URL were detected and removed after delivery.
question_record.question: What is the email address that received the message containing a malicious URL which was later removed after delivery?
solution: A renamed system executable `powershell.exe` was launched on the machine.
A malicious PowerShell Cmdlet was invoked by the user with AadUserId `a2d0f7c2-b0a0-43bd-bce0-27d8ae3be4d0`.
An email containing a malicious URL was delivered and then removed. The recipient was `bjenkins@niseko.alpineskihouse.co`.

27.name: System executable renamed and launched
27.description: A Windows executable file that has been renamed was launched. Attackers might be attempting to use the executable to perform malicious activities, such as running malicious code or connecting to an attacker-controlled network address. By changing the path or file name of a system executable, attackers can avoid certain behavior-based detection technologies that rely on default paths and file names.
